rows.label: Marginal funding goes to lower priority areas (Not specified)
rows.explainer:
GiveWell-funded work by Malaria Consortium makes up roughly 33% of total SMC funding in Chad. See https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uiT6New2aXRB9qyrcQODhflnRR8QOZk-g1_9qaRRqjo/edit#, page 2.

This implies that there would be significant scope to prioritize some areas over other in the absence of GiveWell-directed funding. There appears to be fairly low variation in malaria rates in northern Nigeria: https://malariaatlas.org/explorer/#/

On the other hand, our understanding is that malaria funding is more segmented in Nigeria, and coordinated to a greater degree at the sub-national (state) level than in other countries. This could lead to greater barriers to shifting funding around if a funder were to withdraw support.

How much does it cost the government to increase ln(income) by one unit through education?
rows.explainer:
For comparison, the median GiveWell estimate of cost per unit increase in ln(consumption) for GiveDirectly was $394 (as of November 2017).

We guess that government spending on primary education is roughly as valuable as giving to GiveDirectly, secondary education is roughly 70% as valuable as GiveDirectly, tertiary education is roughly 50% as valuable as giving to GiveDirectly. 

We take weighted averages of these guesses based on actual government expenditure in Uganda.

For more details see: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15_gs-zfPDRnFHs4uWDOJGzo1pccntqIA4XAK5aa4OBA/edit#gid=0)

How much does it cost the government to increase ln(income) by one unit through social security?
rows.explainer:
For comparison, the median GiveWell estimate of cost per unit increase in ln(consumption) for GiveDirectly was $394 (as of November 2017).

We guess that government spending on in-kind social security and social pensions is roughly 70% as valuable as GiveDirectly, and conditional and unconditional cash transfers are roughly as valuable as GiveDirectly. 

We take weighted averages of these guesses based on actual government expenditure in Uganda.

For more details see: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15_gs-zfPDRnFHs4uWDOJGzo1pccntqIA4XAK5aa4OBA/edit#gid=0)

rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
